title: Pens: enclosure, access and a food budget
applies_when: An approved animal-housing project needs a layout.
approach: A pen requires a closed barrier, a usable gate or door, and a pen marker. An ordinary painted zone is not a pen.
Size pasture against observed animal consumption and pen nutrition, not a fixed tile count. Vegetation, season and regrowth matter; bare land can provide little feed even in a large pen.
Keep human crops and hay intended for harvesting outside grazing access. Reserve a route for handling and feed delivery, and room for herd growth.
Keep grazing outdoors. An animal flap can connect a sheltered sleeping area; prepare stored suitable feed for cold seasons when grazing fails.
verify: Native pen recognition, entry access, animal assignment and nutrition supply versus consumption.
reconsider: Animals outgrow the food budget, pasture loses vegetation or winter approaches.
